subject: lavaan command comparable to Mplus "within" statment?

messages.author: a225fe7bebd5f312
messages.subject: lavaan command comparable to Mplus "within" statment?
parts:
Hi All,

I'm curious if lavaan has something similar to the Mplus "within" command.  The within command designates a continuous level 1 variable has having no variance and no covariance at level 2. (Conversely, the "between" command stipulates no variance at level 1.)  Without the within command, any level 1 variable also has a level 2 variance and covariance, even if that variable is not included in the between structure. This behavior is also the default in lavaan.

Now it's easy enough to set the between variance to zero for the level 1 variable in question, but that changes model df.  In addition, the between covariance matrix still features the level 2 variance and covariances for the variable in question, which has ramifications for model fit stats. The Mplus within command retains the level 1 variable in the between covariance matrix but the variance and covariances for the variable are all zero.  

Happy to provide a reproducible example if needed.  Thanks in advance.

Joe

Hi Yves,

Thanks for your reply.  I think there are some discrepancies in the two approaches but I could be wrong.  Here's a reproducible example using data from the Mplus users guide. The within level has simple mediation model in which x2 mediates the relationship between x1 and y.  The variable x1 is within only, as it is not included in the between-level structure.  Variable w is included in the between-level structure but not within.  Mplus syntax would have x1 identified as "within" and w as "between." 

mp9.3.dat <- read.table("https://www.statmodel.com/usersguide/chap9/ex9.3.dat")
names(mp9.3.dat) <- c("u", "y", "x1", "x2", "w", "clus")

mp9.3.l <- '
level: 1
y ~ x2
x2 ~ x1

level: 2
y ~ x2 + w
'

l9.3.out <- sem(mp9.3.l, data=mp9.3.dat, cluster="clus")

summary(l9.3.out, fit.measures=T)

lavInspect(l9.3.out, "cov.ov")

What I find interesting is that the observed covariance matrices do not have the same structure at the different levels (which seems an obvious point): within has x1, x2, and y, and between has w, x2, and y.  Mplus, however, includes w at the within level and x1 at the between (with zero variance and covariance for each).  Here's the lavInspect output:

$within
           y      x2     x1    
y   1.261              
x2  0.443  0.964       
x1 -0.009 -0.019  1.039

$clus
           y      x2     w     
y   0.757              
x2 -0.034  0.021       
w   0.576 -0.003  1.008

And the covariance matrices from Mplus (sampstat) pulled using MplusAutomation:

> med.9.3.out$results$model$sampstat$BETWEEN$covariances
       Y     X2 X1  W
Y   0.76     NA NA NA
X2 -0.03  0.019 NA NA
X1  0.00  0.000  0 NA
W   0.58 -0.002  0  1

> med.9.3.out$results$model$sampstat$WITHIN$covariances
      Y     X2 X1  W
Y  1.26     NA NA NA
X2 0.44  0.965 NA NA
X1 0.23 -0.021  1 NA
W  0.00  0.000  0  0

For the most part, the parameter estimates are the same or close, but the number of estimated free parameters isn't the same.  Model chi-square, baseline chi-square, CFI and RMSEA are the same across the two programs but not SRMR (at both levels) and TLI.  I've attached Mplus output for your perusal.  Thanks in advance for having a look.

Best,

Joe

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan command comparable to Mplus "within" statment?
parts: Hello Joseph,

> What I find interesting is that the observed covariance matrices do not
> have the same structure at the different levels (which seems an obvious
> point): within has x1, x2, and y, and between has w, x2, and y.  Mplus,
> however, includes w at the within level and x1 at the between (with zero
> variance and covariance for each).

That is just a matter of presentation. Internally, lavaan is using the
same matrices as Mplus. But only when we need to combine the two levels
(for computing the loglikelihood) do we 'extend' the matrices to contain
all within+between variables.

> For the most part, the parameter estimates are the same or close, but
> the number of estimated free parameters isn't the same.
I believe the difference is due to this Mplus warning:

*** WARNING in MODEL command
In the MODEL command, the following variable is an x-variable on the
BETWEEN
level and a y-variable on the WITHIN level. This variable will be
treated
as a y-variable on both levels: X2

lavaan is not doing this (yet?). This is indeed a difference. However,
my impression is that Mplus is in fact always using 'fixed.x = FALSE'
when estimating the parameters, but then selectively hides 'exogenous'
fixed.x parameters from the output by default. If you mention them
explicitly in the model specification, the number of free parameter
changes, but the output remains identical:

MODEL:
%WITHIN%
y ON x2;
x2 ON x1;
x1;
%BETWEEN%
y ON x2 w;

w;

So to get output closer to that of Mplus (in terms of parameter
estimates), you can use

fit <- sem(mp9.3.l, data=mp9.3.dat, cluster="clus", fixed.x = FALSE)

The default (in lavaan) is fixed.x = TRUE, and in this case (unlike
Mplus) the exogenous means/variances/covariances are truly fixed to
their sample values. This often leads to small but noticeable differences.

Yves.

messages.author: a225fe7bebd5f312
messages.subject: Re: lavaan command comparable to Mplus "within" statement?
parts:
Thanks again for your reply, Yves. 

Adding "w WITH x2" to the between model in the Mplus code you provided lines up most everything nicely.  Parameter estimates and just about dead on and number of estimated parameters is equal across the two models.  TLI, RMSEA, and SRMR are a tad off, TLI being really off, but I'm not sure why.  Will continue to investigate but I'm pleased that I know what both Mplus and lavaan are doing in those cases.  Makes sense that a term included on the within but not between level should be detected that way by lavaan--not sure why Mplus insists on identifying such variables, unless it's a useful redundancy for the user.

Best,

Joe

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan command comparable to Mplus "within" statement?
parts:
On 7/28/20 6:32 PM, Joseph Bonito wrote:
> know what both Mplus and lavaan are doing in those cases.

Actually, after reflecting on this for a while, I do believe that Mplus
(and not lavaan) is doing the "right thing" in this example. Or at least
almost. If 'x2' occurs at both levels, it should indeed be treated as
'endogenous' implying that we should freely estimate its
variance/intercept at the second level.

Currently, by default, lavaan treats is as 'fixed', because it is
exogenous at level-2. But this fixes the variance/intercept at its
sample estimate: the value you see in lavInspect(fit, "sampstat"). This
is suboptimal. I will change this in dev lavaan.

However, 'x2' is still exogenous (at level-2), and therefore, the
covariance between x2 and w should not be fixed to zero. Which is what
Mplus is now implicitly doing! I will make sure these covariances remain
non-zero.

Thanks for providing this interesting example. I had not considered this
setting before.

Yves.

messages.author: a225fe7bebd5f312
messages.subject: Re: lavaan command comparable to Mplus "within" statement?
parts:
Hi Yves,

You are welcome.  To keep a long story short, I came across it while estimating a model in which two within predictors had the same means at the group level, which is a problem.  The solution was to use only one of the two predictors at the within level while treating the other at as a within-only variable.  Mplus, as we discussed, requires one to do that, which got me wondering how to make lavaan correspond to the Mplus model.  Not that Mplus and its underlying assumptions should be considered the best approach--it shouldn't.  Good to know what's happening under the hood.

Best,

Joe
